contract.note: Coding-oriented design and functionality beyond conversation are fair readings. Whether tool execution qualifies as neurosymbolic remains an interpretation Marcus did not specify; the contract appropriately avoids imposing one.

evidence.note: The contemporaneous company disclosure supports coding-oriented functionality beyond conversation, but does not establish neurosymbolic architecture.

Earlier company disclosure describes coding design and tool execution. Broader applications do not disprove specialization, and applicability of the detailed architecture to June 18 is not established.
The April architectural analysis distinguishes model reasoning from harness execution. It neither verifies the June product state nor settles whether that combination qualifies as neurosymbolic.
The pre-cutoff paper documents definitional uncertainty and proposes a definition; it does not classify Claude Code.

reviews.rationale: Coding-oriented functionality beyond conversation is supported by a contemporaneous company disclosure. The packet does not establish or refute the neurosymbolic classification without choosing an unstated definition, and detailed architectural evidence concerns an earlier version. Non-coding uses and separation of model reasoning from tool execution do not independently contradict the claim.
